laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: AR Code §27-51-1802 — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. The 2023 hands-free law bans all handheld device use while driving. Hands-free mode required.
laws.penalty: $25 first offense, $50 second, $100 third+.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas banned handheld device use while driving in 2023.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §15-42-105 — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Arkansas hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $50; hunting licenses cost approximately $155. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class B misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $500 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Arkansas is a Class B misdemeanor with fines up to $500.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-65-103 — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Arkansas also uses implied consent — refusal triggers automatic license suspension.
laws.penalty: First offense: $150–$1,000 fine, 24–48 hours jail, 6-month license suspension. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Arkansas for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Arkansas is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-71-218 — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. The law applies to both driver and passengers in private vehicles.
laws.penalty: $250 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-64-419 — Recreational cannabis is NOT legal
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Arkansas. Possession of 4 oz or less is a misdemeanor. Medical cannabis is legal since Amendment 98 (2016).
laws.penalty: Possession up to 4 oz: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year. Over 4 oz: felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients with a valid registry ID card are exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Recreational cannabis is not legal in Arkansas; only medical cannabis is permitted.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §20-56-212 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas has a medical cannabis program since 2016 (Amendment 98). Patients may possess up to 2.5 oz per 14 days. Dispensaries operate statewide.
laws.penalty: Non-patients possessing cannabis face criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas has a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Constitutional
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-73-120 — Constitutional state
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas is a constitutional state. Arkansas passed constitutional carry in 2013 (Act 746) allowing permitless carry for eligible adults. Permits still offered for reciprocity.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: Class B misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Arkansas have?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas has constitutional — permitless carry for eligible adults; optional permits available for reciprocity

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Arkansas require a federal NICS background check. Arkansas does not require background checks for private-party gun sales.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas only requires background checks for licensed dealer gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-2-607 — Stand Your Ground
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas has a Stand Your Ground law — no duty to retreat anywhere a person has a legal right to be before using force in self-defense.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a Stand Your Ground law?
options: No — duty to retreat outside home
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has both Stand Your Ground and Castle Doctrine — no duty to retreat.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-4-210 — $11.00/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas's minimum wage is $11.00/hour (2024). Arkansas minimum wage is $11.00/hour (2024), exceeding the federal $7.25.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped employees may have a lower base wage if tips bring them to minimum wage.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's minimum wage is $11.00/hour.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-2-101 — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. Arkansas is an at-will state with public policy and implied contract exceptions.
laws.penalty: N/A — at-will is the default standard.
laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Arkansas employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — Yes
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-3-303 — Arkansas is a right-to-work state
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas is a right-to-work state. Arkansas passed right-to-work in 1944. Union membership cannot be required as a condition of employment.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs labor relations framework.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees and some categories are governed by federal law.

quiz.q: Is Arkansas a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas is a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §4-75-101 — Non-compete enforceability rules
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas courts enforce non-competes if reasonable in scope, duration (typically up to 2 years), and geographic area. Covenants protecting trade secrets are most upheld.
laws.penalty: Overly broad agreements may be voided or reformed by courts.
laws.exceptions: Agreements protecting legitimate trade secrets are most favored.

quiz.q: Are non-compete agreements automatically enforceable in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Courts assess reasonableness of scope, duration, and geography

laws.title: Paid Sick Leave — Not Required
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-4-210 — No statewide mandate
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide paid sick leave requirement. Paid leave is at employer discretion.
laws.penalty: N/A — no mandate exists.
laws.exceptions: Independent contractors are generally not covered.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas require employers to provide paid sick leave?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide paid sick leave mandate — employers set their own policies.

laws.title: Unemployment Insurance
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-10-501 — Unemployment benefits
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $451 for up to 16 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1,000 in the base period.
laws.penalty: Filing fraudulent claims: repayment plus penalties and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Self-employed and independent contractors are generally ineligible for regular UI.

quiz.q: What is the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's maximum weekly unemployment benefit is $451.

laws.title: Workers' Compensation
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-9-401 — Mandatory workers' comp coverage
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas requires employers with 3 or more employees to carry workers' compensation insurance. Covers medical costs and lost wages for work-related injuries.
laws.penalty: Employers without coverage: fines up to $10,000/day, personal liability for claims.
laws.exceptions: Sole proprietors and some domestic workers may be exempt.

quiz.q: How many employees trigger workers' comp requirements in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas requires workers' comp for employers with 3 or more employees.

laws.title: Independent Contractor Classification
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-10-210 — Worker classification rules
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas uses Common law control test to classify workers. Arkansas uses the common law control test for worker classification.
laws.penalty: Misclassification: back taxes, penalties, and retroactive benefits liability.
laws.exceptions: Licensed professionals may have different classification standards.

quiz.q: What test does Arkansas use for worker classification?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas uses the Common law control test for worker classification.

laws.title: Child Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §11-6-101 — Restrictions on youth employment
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas restricts employment of minors. Children under 14: very limited jobs only. Ages 14–15: restricted hours. Most minors under 18 need work permits. Arkansas allows 14-15 year olds to work limited hours outside school; 16-17 have fewer restrictions.
laws.penalty: Employers violating child labor laws: fines up to $10,000 per violation.
laws.exceptions: Family farms and limited entertainment work have exemptions.

quiz.q: At what age do minors generally need work permits in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Most Arkansas minors under 18 need work permits for regular employment.

laws.title: Equal Pay Act
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §16-123-107 — Equal pay for equal work
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits pay discrimination based on sex for substantially equal work. Arkansas Civil Rights Act prohibits pay discrimination based on sex.
laws.penalty: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees for violations.
laws.exceptions: Pay differences justified by seniority, merit, or non-sex factors are permitted.

quiz.q: What agency enforces equal pay laws in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's civil rights agency and the federal EEOC both enforce equal pay laws.

laws.title: Anti-Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §16-123-107 — Protected classes in Arkansas
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits employment discrimination based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, and disability. Sexual orientation and gender identity are NOT explicitly protected in Arkansas state law (only federal Bostock applies).
laws.penalty: Compensatory damages, back pay, reinstatement, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Religious organizations may have limited exemptions for certain positions.

quiz.q: How many employees must an Arkansas employer have before anti-discrimination laws apply?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas anti-discrimination laws apply to employers with 9 or more employees.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice Requirement
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §18-17-602 — 24-hour notice required
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas landlords must give tenants 24 hours' written notice before entering for non-emergency purposes. Emergency entry without notice is allowed.
laws.penalty: Unlawful entry may entitle tenant to damages or lease termination.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies (fire, flood, imminent harm) allow immediate entry without notice.

quiz.q: How many hours notice must Arkansas landlords give before entering?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas landlords must give 24 hours' notice before non-emergency entry.

laws.title: Security Deposit Rules
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §18-17-501 — Two months' rent maximum deposit
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Maximum security deposit is Two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized statement of deductions.
laws.penalty: Landlord who wrongfully withholds deposit may owe double damages plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits for pets may be separate in some cases.

quiz.q: How many days does a Arkansas landlord have to return a security deposit?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas landlords have 30 days to return security deposits after move-out.

laws.title: Rent Control Status — Not Statewide
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §14-16-601 — No statewide rent control; municipalities preempted
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas preempts local rent control — municipalities cannot enact rent stabilization.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/regulatory matter.
laws.exceptions: Federally subsidized housing has separate rent rules.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have statewide rent control?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas state law prohibits local rent control ordinances.

laws.title: Eviction Process & Tenant Protections
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §18-17-901 — Notice and court process required
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas landlords must provide: 3 days notice for nonpayment; 14 days for violations; 30 days for no-cause termination. Court filing required after notice expires.
laws.penalty: Self-help eviction (changing locks, removing belongings) is illegal.
laws.exceptions: Emergency situations may allow expedited proceedings.

quiz.q: How many days notice for non-payment of rent before eviction in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas requires 3 days notice for nonpayment of rent before filing for eviction.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulations
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Varies by city
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: STR regulations vary by municipality. Little Rock and Fayetteville have local ordinances.
laws.penalty: Operating without required licenses: fines and possible closure.
laws.exceptions: Owner-occupied properties renting a single room may have reduced requirements.

quiz.q: Are short-term rentals (Airbnb) regulated in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas regulates STRs primarily at the local level with varying requirements by city.

laws.title: Property Tax
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Average 0.62% effective rate
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.62%. Arkansas has one of the lowest property tax rates in the US.
laws.penalty: Delinquent taxes accrue interest and may result in tax lien or foreclosure.
laws.exceptions: Senior citizens and disabled veterans often receive exemptions. Homestead exemption reduces assessed value.

quiz.q: What is the approximate average effective property tax rate in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.62%.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §26-26-1118 — Up to $375 credit on assessed value homestead exemption
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas homestead exemption provides a property tax credit, not an exemption on full assessed value.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protection for homeowners.
laws.exceptions: Does not protect against tax liens, mortgage foreclosures, or mechanic's liens.

quiz.q: What is Arkansas's homestead exemption?
options: Up to $375 credit on assessed value
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's homestead exemption is Up to $375 credit on assessed value.

laws.title: State Income Tax — Yes — graduated rates
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §26-51-101 — Yes — graduated rates
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has a graduated income tax with rates from 2% to 4.9% (2024). Top rate significantly reduced from 5.9% in recent years.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties, back taxes, and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Federal income taxes apply to all residents regardless of state income tax.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has a graduated income tax up to 4.9%.

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §26-52-101 — 6.5% statewide sales tax
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas has a 6.5% statewide sales tax. Local taxes add an average of 2.1%, making combined rates about 8.6%. Combined state and local rates average 8.6%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties and criminal charges for substantial violations.
laws.exceptions: Exempt items typically include: Prescription drugs and groceries are taxed at a lower rate..

quiz.q: What is the statewide sales tax rate in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's statewide sales tax is 6.5%.

laws.title: Estate / Inheritance Tax — No
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §26-59-101 — No state estate tax
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas repealed its state estate tax. Only federal estate tax applies.
laws.penalty: N/A — federal estate tax applies to all US residents with large estates.
laws.exceptions: Federal estate tax applies to estates over $13 million (2024).

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a state estate or inheritance tax?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no state estate tax.

laws.title: Smoke-Free Workplace Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §20-27-502 — Clean Air Act / Smoke-Free law
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits smoking in most indoor workplaces, restaurants, and public places under the Clean Indoor Air Act of 2006.
laws.penalty: Violation: $100–$500 per incident for individuals.
laws.exceptions: Some private clubs and outdoor areas may be exempt.

quiz.q: Is smoking banned in workplaces and restaurants in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has comprehensive smoke-free workplace laws for most indoor spaces.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-20-104 — Helmets required for all riders
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas requires helmets for all motorcycle operators and passengers regardless of age.
laws.penalty: Helmet violation: $100 fine.
laws.exceptions: N/A — all riders must wear helmets.

quiz.q: Who must wear a motorcycle helmet in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas requires helmets for all motorcycle riders.

laws.title: Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-37-702 — Mandatory seatbelts
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas requires all front-seat occupants to wear seatbelts. All passengers under 15 must be buckled. Children under 8 or under 60 lbs must be in child safety seats.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for violations; higher for child restraint violations.
laws.exceptions: Some commercial vehicles and emergency situations may have limited exemptions.

quiz.q: Is the seatbelt law a primary offense in Arkansas?
options: Yes, police can stop for seatbelt alone
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's seatbelt law is a primary enforcement offense.

laws.title: Speed Limits
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-51-601 — Statutory speed limits
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Residential: 30 mph; highways: 65 mph; interstates: 70 mph; school zones: 25 mph. Arkansas maximum interstate speed is 75 mph in some rural areas.
laws.penalty: Speeding fines start at $50 and increase with severity; reckless driving is a criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt when responding.

quiz.q: What is the interstate speed limit in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's standard interstate speed limit is 70 mph.

laws.title: Texting While Driving
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-51-1802 — Hands-free law — all handheld use banned
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas bans all handheld device use while driving (texting, calling, browsing).
laws.penalty: First offense: $25; repeat: $100.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are permitted while driving.

quiz.q: Is texting while driving banned in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas banned all handheld device use while driving (2023).

laws.title: DUI Checkpoint Legality
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-24-201 — Sobriety checkpoints permitted
laws.fullDescription: DUI sobriety checkpoints are legal in Arkansas. DUI checkpoints are legal in Arkansas when conducted with proper procedures and public notice.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines when checkpoints are legal.
laws.exceptions: Checkpoints must follow established procedures to be constitutional.

quiz.q: Are DUI sobriety checkpoints legal in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: DUI checkpoints are legal with proper procedures.

laws.title: Move Over Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-51-308 — Slow or move over for emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas's Move Over Law requires drivers to change lanes or slow down when passing stopped emergency vehicles and tow trucks and highway maintenance vehicles with flashing lights on the roadway or shoulder.
laws.penalty: Violation: $500 fine; if injury or death results, criminal charges may apply.
laws.exceptions: Required only when safe to do so without creating greater hazard.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas's Move Over Law cover tow trucks?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's Move Over Law covers tow trucks.

laws.title: Cell Phone Use While Driving
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §27-51-1802 — Handheld device restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Beyond texting, Arkansas bans all handheld device use (2023 law), including calls, texting, and browsing. Hands-free only.
laws.penalty: Fines range from $25 to $100.
laws.exceptions: Hands-free calls and navigation use are generally permitted.

quiz.q: Can drivers make calls on a handheld phone while driving in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas bans all handheld phone use while driving, including hands-held calls.

laws.title: Age of Majority
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §9-25-101 — Age 18 is legal adulthood
laws.fullDescription: In Arkansas, the age of majority is 18. At 18, residents gain the right to vote, enter contracts, and make their own legal decisions. Minors may be emancipated by court order. Age-specific restrictions (alcohol, cannabis) still apply.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines civil rights.
laws.exceptions: Some rights have higher age thresholds: alcohol (21), cannabis where legal (21).

quiz.q: What is the age of majority in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's age of majority is 18, consistent with most US states.

laws.title: Voting Rights & Restoration
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §7-5-201 — Voter eligibility and felon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Felons lose voting rights during incarceration and parole/probation. Rights are automatically restored upon completion of full sentence.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible (while incarcerated): criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Mentally incapacitated persons adjudicated incompetent may lose voting rights.

quiz.q: When are voting rights restored to a felon in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Voting rights restored automatically after completing full sentence including parole.

laws.title: Jury Duty Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §16-31-201 — Jury service
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas citizens who are US citizens, 18+, registered voters (or driver's license holders) may be called for jury duty. Jurors receive $50/day. Employers must allow employees to serve.
laws.penalty: Willfully ignoring a jury summons: contempt of court, fines up to $500.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions include active military, police, extreme hardship, and some medical conditions.

quiz.q: What is the daily pay for jurors in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas jurors receive $50 per day for service.

laws.title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §12-18-402 — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas requires certain professionals (teachers, doctors, social workers, law enforcement, etc.) to report suspected child abuse. Not a universal reporter state. Reports must be made to child protective services or law enforcement. Good-faith reporters are protected from liability.
laws.penalty: Failure to report known child abuse: Class A misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege may apply in limited circumstances.

quiz.q: Who must report suspected child abuse in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas requires designated professionals to report suspected child abuse.

laws.title: Age of Consent
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-14-125 — Age of consent is 16
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas's age of consent is 16. Sexual activity with a person under 16 by someone 3+ years older is a crime. Sex offenders must register with the state registry.
laws.penalty: Sexual abuse of a minor: Class A felony with mandatory sex offender registration..
laws.exceptions: Romeo and Juliet provision: Close-in-age exemption applies for persons within 3 years of age..

quiz.q: What is the age of consent in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's age of consent is 16.

laws.title: Emancipation of Minors
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §9-27-362 — Court-ordered emancipation
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation, granting adult legal status. The court considers whether it's in the minor's best interests and whether the minor can support themselves.
laws.penalty: N/A — emancipation is a civil court process.
laws.exceptions: Emancipation does not override minimum age laws for alcohol, cannabis, or voting.

quiz.q: At what minimum age can a minor petition for emancipation in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation.

laws.title: Curfew Laws for Minors
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Local ordinances only
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: No statewide curfew. Municipalities set their own curfew ordinances. Little Rock has a midnight curfew for minors under 18.
laws.penalty: Curfew violation: minor taken into custody and released to parents; parents may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Minors with employment, parental supervision, or school activities are typically exempt.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a statewide youth curfew?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide curfew; local municipalities set their own rules.

laws.title: Corporal Punishment in Schools
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §6-18-505 — Corporal punishment permitted
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas permits corporal punishment in public schools (one of fewer than 20 states that still allows it). Must be reasonable and administered by authorized personnel.
laws.penalty: Educators using prohibited corporal punishment face administrative discipline and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Physical restraint to prevent imminent harm is permitted.

quiz.q: Is corporal punishment allowed in Arkansas public schools?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas is one of the few states that still permits corporal punishment in public schools.

laws.title: Homeschooling Regulations
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §6-15-501 — Homeschooling requirements
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Families must file a notice of intent to homeschool with the local district, cover required subjects (English, math, science, social studies, etc.), and submit annual assessments.
laws.penalty: Failure to provide required education: mandatory enrollment in public school.
laws.exceptions: Some states have additional oversight or assessment requirements.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have strict homeschooling regulations?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas has moderate-regulation homeschooling with annual notice, required subjects, and annual assessments.

laws.title: School Vaccination Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §6-18-702 — Required vaccinations for school entry
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas requires students to be vaccinated against standard childhood diseases for school entry. Students must be vaccinated or have a qualified exemption. Arkansas allows religious and medical exemptions.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated students without exemptions may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions available: medical and religious exemptions.

quiz.q: Can Arkansas parents claim a philosophical exemption from school vaccinations?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas vaccination exemptions: medical and religious exemptions.

laws.title: Abortion Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-61-202 — Near-total abortion ban
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has a near-total abortion ban (Act 180 of 2021) with very limited exceptions. The ban took effect after Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization (2022). Abortions are only permitted to save the life of the mother.
laws.penalty: Performing an abortion: Class D felony (up to 6 years).
laws.exceptions: Medical emergencies to save the life of the mother are typically exempt.

quiz.q: What is the gestational limit on abortion in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has a near-total abortion ban with only a narrow exception to save the mother's life.

laws.title: Death Penalty — Authorized
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-4-617 — Death penalty status
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas has the death penalty. Arkansas authorizes the death penalty for capital murder. After a long pause, Arkansas carried out executions in 2017.
laws.penalty: Death penalty crimes: Capital murder.
laws.exceptions: Federal death penalty may apply to federal crimes regardless of state law.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have the death penalty?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has the death penalty; capital murder is punishable by death.

laws.title: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID)
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-10-106 — Assisted suicide is illegal
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Medical aid in dying is not legal in Arkansas. Assisting a suicide is a Class C felony.
laws.penalty: Assisting a suicide: Class C felony (up to 10 years).
laws.exceptions: Withdrawal of life support and palliative sedation are legal with patient consent everywhere.

quiz.q: Is medical aid in dying (assisted suicide) legal in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Medical aid in dying is illegal in Arkansas.

laws.title: Drug Penalties (Non-Cannabis)
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-64-419 — Controlled Substances Act
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas controlled substance penalties: Schedule I possession (heroin, meth, cocaine) is a Class A or B felony. Drug courts and diversion programs are available for first-time offenders.
laws.penalty: Possession of hard drugs: Class A or B felony (up to 20 years depending on schedule). Distribution/manufacture: Class A or Y felony (up to life for schedule I distribution).
laws.exceptions: Prescribed medications used as directed are exempt.

quiz.q: Is simple drug possession a felony in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas drug penalties vary by schedule — possession of hard drugs is a Class A or B felony.

laws.title: Asset Forfeiture Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-64-505 — Civil asset forfeiture
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas allows civil asset forfeiture for drug crimes and some other offenses without a criminal conviction. Reform efforts have increased some protections.
laws.penalty: N/A — forfeiture is an action against property.
laws.exceptions: Innocent owner defense available: property returned if owner proves no criminal connection.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas require a criminal conviction before forfeiture?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas allows civil asset forfeiture without requiring a criminal conviction.

laws.title: Expungement & Record Sealing
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §16-90-601 — Expungement availability
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas allows sealing of certain misdemeanor and non-violent felony records after a waiting period. First-time offenders have better options.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a post-conviction relief process.
laws.exceptions: Serious felonies, sex offenses, and violent crimes generally cannot be expunged.

quiz.q: Can first-time non-violent offenders expunge their records in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas allows record sealing for certain non-violent offenses.

laws.title: Solitary Confinement Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §12-27-101 — Restricted housing policies
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas DOC has policies on restricted housing. Some reforms limit solitary for juveniles and the mentally ill.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs prison administration.
laws.exceptions: Extremely dangerous inmates may face longer restricted housing.

quiz.q: Has Arkansas restricted the use of solitary confinement?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Limited reforms restrict solitary confinement for vulnerable populations.

laws.title: Private Prison Use
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §12-27-101 — Private correctional facilities
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas uses some private prison facilities including federal contract facilities.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy issue.
laws.exceptions: Some community corrections facilities are privately operated under state contracts.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas use privately operated prisons?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas uses some privately contracted facilities for portions of its prison population.

laws.title: Police Body Camera Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §12-27-113 — Body camera law
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide body camera mandate. The State Police uses body cameras; local departments set their own policies.
laws.penalty: Violations handled by department policy and state oversight.
laws.exceptions: Individual agencies may have stricter policies than state law requires.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a statewide body camera law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: No statewide body camera mandate; departments set their own policies.

laws.title: Police Use-of-Force Policies
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-2-601 — Justified use of force
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas law: deadly force is only justified when an officer reasonably believes it necessary to prevent death or serious physical injury to the officer or another.
laws.penalty: Unjustified use of force: potential criminal charges and civil liability.
laws.exceptions: Force always subject to the reasonableness standard.

quiz.q: When may Arkansas officers use deadly force?
options: When reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury
quiz.explanation: Arkansas officers may use deadly force only when reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury.

laws.title: Red Flag Law (ERPO) — No
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-73-101 — Extreme Risk Protection Orders
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas does not have a Red Flag (ERPO) law. Arkansas does not have a Red Flag law. Bills have been proposed but not passed.
laws.penalty: N/A — ERPO is a civil court order, not a criminal penalty.
laws.exceptions: Existing domestic violence protective orders may include firearm surrender in all states.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a Red Flag (ERPO) law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas does not have an Extreme Risk Protection Order law.

laws.title: Hate Crime Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-71-208 — Bias-motivated crime laws
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas has a hate crime statute providing sentencing enhancements for crimes motivated by race, religion, color, national origin, or ancestry.
laws.penalty: Hate crime enhancement or separate charge: up to an additional 5 years added to the base sentence..
laws.exceptions: Protected speech expressing bias without accompanying criminal conduct is constitutionally protected.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have hate crime laws?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has a hate crime enhancement law covering race, religion, national origin, and color.

laws.title: Domestic Violence Laws & Protections
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §9-15-201 — Domestic Violence Act
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has comprehensive domestic violence laws including protective orders, 72-hour emergency custody, and mandatory arrest policies for DV assault.
laws.penalty: Violation of DV protective order: Class A misdemeanor; repeat violations escalate to felony..
laws.exceptions: Mutual protective orders may be issued in some circumstances.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence with probable cause.

laws.title: Stalking & Cyberstalking Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-71-229 — Stalking prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits stalking — repeated non-consensual contact causing substantial distress. First-degree stalking (involving weapon or violation of protective order) is a Class C felony. Second-degree is a Class A misdemeanor. Electronic harassment is covered.
laws.penalty: First-degree stalking: Class C felony (up to 10 years). Second-degree: Class A misdemeanor (up to 1 year).
laws.exceptions: Lawful investigations by law enforcement are not considered stalking.

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking (electronic harassment) covered by Arkansas's stalking law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's stalking law covers cyberstalking through electronic means.

laws.title: Consumer Data Privacy Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §4-110-101 — Data breach notification law only
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has a data breach notification law requiring businesses to notify residents of security breaches. No comprehensive consumer privacy law yet.
laws.penalty: Data breach notification: civil fines up to $10,000 per violation per day.
laws.exceptions: Small businesses may have reduced obligations under some state laws.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a comprehensive consumer data privacy law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas only has breach notification rules, not a comprehensive consumer privacy law.

laws.title: Social Media Age Verification
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §N/A — No state law
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no social media age verification law. Federal efforts may address this.
laws.penalty: N/A — enforcement mechanisms vary.
laws.exceptions: Federal platforms regulation may preempt state laws.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas require age verification for social media?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no social media age verification law.

laws.title: Environmental Regulations
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §8-4-103 — Environmental protection
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: The Arkansas Department of Energy and Environment (DEE) and Department of Health regulate air, water, and waste. Oil and gas drilling, agricultural runoff, and industrial emissions are regulated.
laws.penalty: Environmental violations: civil fines up to $25,000/day; criminal penalties for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: Some agricultural and industrial uses have specific permitting pathways.

quiz.q: Which agency enforces environmental laws in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas's state environmental agency works alongside the EPA to enforce environmental laws.

laws.title: Renewable Energy Standards
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §23-18-601 — Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has a voluntary renewable energy goal but no binding Renewable Portfolio Standard. The state relies heavily on natural gas and some coal.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/utility requirement, not a criminal law.
laws.exceptions: Utilities that miss RPS targets may pay alternative compliance payments.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has only a voluntary renewable energy goal, not a binding RPS.

laws.title: Plastic Bag Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §8-9-101 — No statewide ban or fee
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide plastic bag ban or fee.
laws.penalty: Retailer violations: N/A.
laws.exceptions: Bags for meat, produce, or bulk items are often exempt.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a statewide plastic bag ban or fee?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no statewide plastic bag law.

laws.title: Bottle Deposit Law
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §8-9-201 — Bottle bill status
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no bottle deposit/redemption program.
laws.penalty: Retailers not accepting returns may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Some municipal redemption centers supplement mandatory deposit systems.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a bottle deposit/redemption law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has no bottle deposit program.

laws.title: Animal Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-62-103 — Animal cruelty prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas prohibits cruelty to animals including torture, beating, neglect, and fighting. Intentional torture or killing is a Class D felony. Organized dog fighting is a Class D felony. Neglect is a Class A misdemeanor.
laws.penalty: Intentional cruelty: Class D felony (up to 6 years). Neglect: Class A misdemeanor (up to 1 year).
laws.exceptions: Lawful hunting, fishing, pest control, and veterinary procedures are exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for intentional animal cruelty in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Intentional animal cruelty is punishable by Class D felony (up to 6 years).

laws.title: Exotic Pet Ownership
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-62-103 — Exotic and wild animal ownership
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas prohibits ownership of inherently dangerous wild animals (big cats, bears, venomous snakes, crocodilians) without a permit. Permits are available for accredited facilities.
laws.penalty: Unlawful possession of prohibited animal: Class A misdemeanor; animal seizure..
laws.exceptions: Licensed zoos, wildlife rehabilitators, and research institutions may keep otherwise prohibited animals.

quiz.q: Are large exotic cats (lions, tigers) legal as pets in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Large exotic cats may be possessed with appropriate permits in Arkansas.

laws.title: Fireworks Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §20-22-702 — Consumer fireworks regulations
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas is one of the more permissive states for fireworks — consumer aerial fireworks (bottle rockets, aerial shells) are legal statewide. Local ordinances may restrict certain uses.
laws.penalty: Fireworks violation: $500–$2,000 fines plus liability for fire damage.
laws.exceptions: Licensed pyrotechnic operators may use professional-grade fireworks at permitted events.

quiz.q: Are consumer aerial fireworks legal in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas allows consumer aerial fireworks statewide (subject to local ordinances).

laws.title: Gambling Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §5-66-101 — Gambling regulations
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has multiple casinos after Amendment 100 (2018) legalized commercial gaming. Currently 4 licensed casinos operate. A state lottery also exists.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: Illegal gambling: Class A misdemeanor..
laws.exceptions: Charitable gaming (bingo, pull tabs) for nonprofits typically permitted with license.

quiz.q: Are commercial casinos legal in Arkansas?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: Arkansas has commercial casinos after voters approved gambling in 2018.

laws.title: Net Neutrality (State Level)
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §N/A — Internet regulation
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no state net neutrality law.
laws.penalty: N/A — enforcement varies by state.
laws.exceptions: Federal FCC rules may preempt conflicting state laws.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a state net neutrality law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: No state net neutrality law exists in Arkansas.

laws.title: Right to Repair Laws
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §N/A — Consumer right to repair
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: Arkansas has no right-to-repair law.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines consumer rights.
laws.exceptions: Some manufacturers have voluntarily expanded repair access independent of state laws.

quiz.q: Does Arkansas have a right-to-repair law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: No right-to-repair law in Arkansas.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Employment Protections
laws.subtitle: Ark. Code Ann. §16-123-107 — Sexual orientation and gender identity protections
laws.fullDescription: Arkansas: LGBTQ+ workers are not explicitly protected by Arkansas state law. Federal Bostock v. Clayton County (2020) extends Title VII protections nationwide.
laws.penalty: Employment discrimination based on LGBTQ+ status: same remedies as other protected classes.
laws.exceptions: The federal Bostock v. Clayton County (2020) ruling extended Title VII to cover LGBTQ+ workers nationwide.

quiz.q: Are LGBTQ+ workers explicitly protected by Arkansas state law?
quiz.explanation: Arkansas: LGBTQ+ workers rely on federal Bostock protections; Arkansas has no explicit state law covering sexual orientation or gender identity in employment.
